text:
maya: Heads-up — provisioning in us-west1 is hanging on serial console for a subset of GPU racks (rack-a3, rack-a4). ~12 nodes stuck in BIOS init and never hit OS.
kevin: Ugh. Any recent BMC/BIOS changes for those racks?
maya: We had a BMC roll yesterday evening targeting sensor flaps. Logs show repeated 'oobd: tx queue full' and then UEFI messages about secure boot state flips. Short log snippet:```
Nov 18 03:05:12 oobd[2441]: tx_queue_full drop=42 queue_depth=1983
Nov 18 03:05:13 bmc-fw: ledg_state=0x4 nvram_checksum=0x1f7
Nov 18 03:05:14 uefi: SecureBoot variable changed from 1 -> 0
Nov 18 03:05:15 host: watchdog triggered, holding at BIOS POST
```
olivia: @raj did your rollout touch secureboot/ledger handling? :eyes:
raj: I pushed BMC 2024.11.7 to address sensor reboots and a UART buffering bug. The rollout notes didn't mention secure boot toggles. I see the deploy job finished across west yesterday — ops-bot shows job id 5423. Investigating logs now.
ops-bot: deploy job 5423 finished - 2024-11-18T03:12:02Z - target: us-west1-bmc-patch - success on 120/132 hosts - 12 failures
liam: quick repro: ssh via oob proxy to node-122 then `screen /dev/ttyS1 115200` — you see repeated: `tx queue full` then console freeze.
kevin: Sounds like oob-proxy is rate-limiting/buffering badly under new fw behaviour. If proxy drops console packets, host POST can timeout and UEFI falls back toggling variables.
maya: Mitigation idea: increase oob-proxy tx queue and throttle update concurrency so BMCs aren't hit with bursts. Also pause further rollouts in west.
raj: Agree. I'm preparing a patch: reduce rollout batch to 5, add 15s stagger between hosts, and skip nodes with GPUs under allocation pressure.
olivia: Customer impact — provisioning delays are causing reserved capacity shortfall for a few infra customers. Estimated cost delta ~+$2000/day if this continues. Filing incident: INC-2024-WUS-BMC-03 and looping Customer Success. :shield:
kevin: Temporary mitigation for canary: `systemctl stop oob-proxy; edit /etc/oob/proxy.conf set tx_queue=2048; systemctl start oob-proxy` on west1-canary, then monitor `oobctl metrics`. If queue drops and drops==0, slowly roll out config.
liam: Ran `oobctl metrics` on canary: `queue_depth=1968 tx_rate=612/s drops_total=4512 last_1h` — high but stable. After bumping to 2048, queue_depth fell to ~320 within 2m.
maya: Good. Can someone run `oobctl dump-logs --since 2024-11-18T02:50Z | grep -i "SecureBoot"` and paste limited output? We need to confirm if toggles are a side-effect or a separate bug.
raj: Pasted relevant lines to thread. TL;DR: a small NV write sequence from BMC during sensor init is flipping UEFI var when combined with packet drops. I suspect the BMC FW write ordering changed.
olivia: Plan: rollback the BMC FW on the 12 impacted hosts during a maintenance window at 04:00 UTC, apply oob-proxy queue bump cluster-wide as hotfix, and then re-run a controlled slim rollout with batch=5 and extra validation. Inform CS and affected customers.
maya: I'll own the rollback window and the runbook. Draft runbook steps: 1) cordon affected nodes, 2) attach serial, 3) flash bmc 2024.10.2, 4) validate `oobctl metrics` drops==0 and `ipmitool chassis status` healthy, 5) uncordon.
kevin: Add step: monitor `redwood-console` provisioning latency metric and `reserved-capacity` alerts for 1h post-uncordon.
liam: Also add check for `UEFI variable SecureBoot` value via `uefi-tools` after boot.
ops-bot: incident INC-2024-WUS-BMC-03 created by olivia. Priority: P2. Pager notified.
raj: I'll open a bug for FW ordering with vendor and request hotfix. Also PR to oob-proxy to improve backpressure handling so drops don't coincide with NV writes.
maya: Thanks everyone. Posting runbook and timeline in #incidents. Will update here after rollback. :thumbsup:
